score_notes.novelty: Letter case as source-vs-render target is genuinely new to the catalogue, but the one-line CSS + ledger + cartel pattern is now a familiar DNA subgenre alongside Silencio, La Disparition, Quotation, Incipit, Non-finito, Indivisible, Rubrica, and Schreibzeit — fresh target, seen pairing.
score_notes.nuance: Surface gag (a monument that brags it cannot be copied, copied in one keystroke) lands through the copy interaction alone; literate reading (Horace's boast vs Benjamin's aura) deepens it without needing the cartel; the "un-chisel" toggle makes the construction's reversibility the witty closer.
score_notes.narrative: Explicitly names and answers Silencio and La Disparition and the value/authenticity axis is staged through the endowment inscription, but the chance/order axis is absent and the broader source-vs-render extension is stated in the cartel rather than enacted through a structural surprise.
score_notes.craft: The build is tight — single CSS declaration, one toggle, one programmatic select, live ledger via selectionchange/copy; the stele styling and incised text-shadow serve the metaphor without bloat; nothing to remove, nothing obviously missing.
score_notes.wit: "A monument more lasting than a keystroke" and "you may take nothing from this room" (which you do, in lowercase) land the joke through mechanism; the ledger's "0 capital letters in the source" is the deflation that closes it; humor rides the CSS rather than sitting beside it.

references_named: Horace, Odes III.30 (exegi monumentum aere perennius), 23 BC
Trajan's Column / Roman monumental capitals (capitalis monumentalis)
Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
rationale: The mechanism (text-transform:uppercase with a live attestation that nothing uppercase lives in the DOM or the clipboard) cleanly enacts the conceptual point: monumentality and the aura of the carved capital are a single render pass, not substance. The Horace + Benjamin pairing is well-chosen and the un-chisel toggle is the witty minimal gesture the DNA rewards. The work is materially distinct from every catalogued item (no prior work uses letter case as the source-vs-render target) and the ethics, attribution and voice are clean.
reservations: The one-line-CSS + live-ledger + cartel structure is now a recognizable y-a-v-a subgenre (Silencio, La Disparition, Quotation, Incipit, Non-finito, Indivisible, Rubrica, Schreibzeit, Rivers), so the work's novel contribution is the case target rather than the form. The chance/order axis is absent — the work lives entirely on the value/authenticity axis — which limits the narrative depth even though the lineage is correctly named.
revision_suggestion: Consider folding the chance/order axis into the carving itself — for instance, letting a once-seeded RNG occasionally drop a capital that breaks the lowercase contract (so the monument's own 'authenticity' is visibly chance-driven), or having a per-visit 'weathering' of the inscription that thins letters on the order-axis side. That would extend the twenty-year argument with a move the source-vs-render family has not made and would move the work toward the 'strong' threshold.
